claims.label: Rooftop footage depicts a movement identified by host as lateral/military crawl
claims.claim: The footage shown depicts an individual performing what the host identifies, with reference to a side-by-side military reference clip, as a "lateral crawl."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original unaltered footage, authenticate source chain, and have independent military-tactics experts assess whether the movement matches the lateral-crawl technique as shown in the reference clip.

claims.label: Rooftop footage shows no clearly visible muzzle flash
claims.claim: During the rooftop segment held before the shooter rises to flee, no muzzle flash is clearly visible in the displayed footage.
claims.investigative_direction: Submit original footage for frame-by-frame forensic analysis and compare with reference muzzle-flash signatures for the alleged weapon type.

claims.label: Rooftop footage shows no visible recoil/kickback
claims.claim: In the displayed footage, the shooter is not shown exhibiting visible recoil or kickback consistent with the alleged weapon (German 98 Mouser family heirloom) at the moment of firing.
claims.investigative_direction: Frame-by-frame forensic review of original footage; cross-reference with recoil physics of the alleged firearm model.

claims.label: A back-and-forth flash is visible during the rooftop crawl
claims.claim: A flash or back-and-forth light phenomenon is visible in the rooftop footage during the individual's crawl.
claims.investigative_direction: Slow-motion forensic review of original footage to determine whether the flash is environmental (reflective surface, vehicle light) or item-related (signal mirror, flag, etc.).

claims.label: Wikipedia article on John C. Phelan contains a "Relationship with Jeffrey Epstein" subsection
claims.claim: The displayed Wikipedia article on John C. Phelan (Secretary of the Navy) contains a tab/subsection titled "Relationship with Jeffrey Epstein."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify current Wikipedia article state at archive.org snapshots and cross-reference with original Epstein document releases.

claims.label: Wikipedia states Phelan flew on Epstein's plane on February 27, 2006 (JFK to Luton)
claims.claim: The Wikipedia article states that Phelan flew on Jeffrey Epstein's plane on February 27, 2006, from JFK International Airport to London Luton Airport, per passenger manifests released by the U.S. House Committee in October 2025.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify against the released October 2025 House Committee manifest documents.

claims.label: Wikipedia states Phelan flew with Jean-Luc Brunel on Epstein's plane on March 3, 2006
claims.claim: The Wikipedia article states that Phelan flew on Epstein's plane on March 3, 2006, from London to New York, with twelve other passengers including modeling agent Jean-Luc Brunel, per the released manifest.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify against released October 2025 House Committee manifest documents and cross-reference Brunel's known 2006 travel.

claims.label: Tyler Robinson texted that he was "hoping that pooch has a bad sniffer"

claims.label: Becca proposes bullet fragments could have been lodged in gauze placed in Charlie Kirk's wound
claims.claim: Viewer Becca proposes that bullet fragments potentially lodged in gauze placed in Charlie Kirk's wound could account for bullet-mismatch findings, asking whether the gloves seen at the door were related. Host acknowledges possibility but suggests a medical-examiner-route alternative.
claims.investigative_direction: Review medical examiner reports and chain-of-custody records for any gauze or material handling; verify bullet-fragment provenance.

claims.label: Jacob Morrison asserts rooftop flash is a position signal; host concurs action appears professional
claims.claim: Viewer Jacob Morrison asserts the rooftop flash is a signal that the shooter was in position. Host concurs: "Sure did look like a professional."
